hypothesis: A coherent event clock plus finite polling safeguards prevent malformed injected test clocks from generating unbounded operations logs without changing the real rental deadline or normal30second cadence.
changes: Event elapsed times use the same injected clock as the controller.
Constant clock plus no-op wait fails after three immediate non-progress polls; slower stalls use a300second monotonic bound.
Poll count capped at ceil(initial remaining rental seconds/30)+4, catching a near-frozen clock that otherwise resets the stall check.
Poll ceiling follows the existing remote stop path; exact selected-pod release remains in outer finally.
Successful fake lifecycle tests use a coherent advancing clock/sleep pair.
Constant and micro-advancing regressions run in subprocesses with10second timeouts and parent-owned temporary directories.
negative_case_assertions: missing durable job exit cannot make the fake operation poll forever
fewer than33 event rows and less than16KiB log per malformed-clock fixture
elapsed times use injected clock rather than fake origin/real epoch mismatch
subprocess killed and reaped on timeout; parent owns temp cleanup
scope: Local metadata/dummy subprocess fixtures only. No ML, rendering, paid API, GPU or provider operations.
next_decision: Use this clock-safe controller in subsequent Linux campaign handoffs. Existing actual training/runtime assertions remain pending; metadata tests are not an RL quality result.
